To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the PF technique is an efficient and robust method to study the evolution of the phase space distribution in the strong beam‐beam regime.

the evolution of the phase space distribution of two colliding beam systems, in the absence diffusion and damping, can be described using the PF operator technique, that the phase space distribution is not Gaussian, and that the phase space density is not conserved.
we developed a parallel code for the numerical calculation of the evolution of the phase space density of colliding beams, using the PF operator technique.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and implementation of a new parallel code, which is based on the PF operator technique, to solve the 4D Liouville’s equation of the beam‐beam interaction.
the numerical calculation of the phase space density of a two‐beam system in the presence of a collective beam‐beam interaction.
the numerical solution of a nonlinear, nonautonomous, nonlocal evolution equation for a probability density function (pdf) in a 4D phase-space.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PF operator technique, as applied in the present study, is a very powerful and efficient numerical method for the study of the beam‐beam interaction.

, for a wide variety of beam‐beam interaction scenarios, the PF operator method is an accurate, fast, and reliable method for calculating the evolution of the phase space density of a colliding beam system.

this code is able to reproduce the phase space density evolution of two colliding beam bunches, which are coupled by the collective beam‐beam interaction and in the absence of any diffusion or damping effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the code is capable of simulating the beam evolution in the phase space for the strong‐strong beam beam interaction in the case of two counter‐rotating colliding beams, in the absence diffusion and damping, with a good precision.
we developed a numerical method for solving the Fokker‐Planck equation, which is the equation of motion of the 4-D phase space density of a beam.
, for the first time, we have developed a code that can be used to calculate the evolution for a general initial distribution of the two beams in the phase space.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PF operator technique can be applied to the beam‐beam problem in a straightforward manner.
we are able to obtain accurate numerical solutions of the phase space density for the strong‐strong beam beam interaction.
the PF technique can be extended to the 4D case and that the resulting code scales very well on a large number of processors.
